items.title: 【重要通知】MindSpore 后端"日落计划"已启动：MindSpeed-LLM 停止 MindSpore 框架支持
items.bodyExcerpt:
# **问题背景**

为聚焦资源保障 PyTorch 后端的持续演进，MindSpeed 套件已正式启动 **MindSpore 后端"日落计划"**：停止 MindSpore 框架后端的开发与支持，MindSpeed-LLM 仓库将移除 MindSpore 相关代码、文档、示例与测试。

**此举措旨在：**

- 聚焦维护精力：将有限的社区维护资源集中在活跃度更高的 PyTorch 后端上。
- 降低使用成本：避免用户在两套后端间选择与适配时产生额外负担。
- 保持仓库健康：移除已停止演进的适配层，减少存量代码的维护与门禁成本。

我们称此计划为"日落计划"，象征着对完成使命的 MindSpore 后端致以谢意并优雅地告别。

# **主要举措**

- 删除 `docs/zh/mindspore`、`docs/en/mindspore`（MindSpore 安装/快速入门/支持模型文档）
- 删除 `examples/mindspore`（llama2 / llama3 / glm4 / deepseek2 / deepseek3 / qwen 系列 / qwen3_moe 等 MindSpore 训练与转换示例）
- 删除 `mindspeed_llm/mindspore`（MindSpore 后端适配包）与 `tests/mindspore`（0day / ST 测试）
- 删除 `mindspeed_llm/features_manager/ai_framework`（`--ai-framework mindspore` 特性注册）与 `ci/access_control_test_ms.py`
- `rlhf_gpt.py`：移除 MindSpore 分支，RLHF 固定使用默认 `RayActorGroup` launcher
- `README.md` / `README_en.md` 移除 MindSpore 支持公告条目

**对应变更 MR**：https://gitcode.com/Ascend/MindSpeed-LLM/merge_requests/5058

# **影响说明**

- `--ai-framework mindspore` 参数不再支持，MindSpore 后端文档、示例与测试一并移除
- **PyTorch 后端完全不受影响**，pretrain / finetune / RLHF 各入口用法不变
- 套件内其他仓库同步日落：MindSpeed（!3993）、MindSpeed-MM（!3159，公告 issue [#717](https://gitcode.com/Ascend/MindSpeed-MM/issues/717)）、MindSpeed-Core-MS（!764）

# **用户指引**

如您仍在使用 MindSpeed-LLM 的 MindSpore 后端，请在本 issue 下留言说明使用场景，我们将评估并协助迁移；对 PyTorch 后端的使用无任何影响。

感谢每一位曾经为 MindSpore 后端贡献代码与反馈问题的开发者。

items.title: feat: support GLM5.2 LoRA training and checkpoint correctness
items.bodyExcerpt:
## What this PR does / why we need it?


  完善 GLM5.2 原生 LoRA 训练的参数结构、并行梯度处理及 checkpoint 保存与加载，解决专家参数归约不完整、MLA 输入梯度缺失和训练状态保存不完整等问题。

  主要修改：

  - 支持 Q/KV 独立 A：在原生 PEFT LoRA 中为 Q、KV 分别维护可训练的 A 矩阵，保留原有 B 的输出分块。新增参数在 DDP 和优化器初始化前注册，克隆初值不额外消耗随机数。
  - 修正专家并行梯度：补齐专家 LoRA 参数的 expert-DP 属性，区分 ETP 复制参数与分片参数，对复制参数累加各特征分片产生的梯度。
  - 补齐 MLA 的 TP 输入梯度：在 absorb 路径中保留 SP gather 行为，并为非 SP 的 TP 场景补充 KV 输入梯度求和。
  - 修正非均匀 PP 层号：补齐新版 Megatron 全局层偏移函数的注册，避免非均匀分层时出现层编号及 DSA 共享关系错位。
  - 完善 checkpoint 正确性：LoRA checkpoint 保留训练期间更新的 router bias；首次加载底座及 adapter 重载前将对应 buffer 保持为 FP32，避免复制过程中的精度损失；修复 swap optimizer 场景下保存时读取已释放设备存储的问题。

  相关实现通过 MindSpeed-LLM 的 feature 机制接入，无需修改 MindSpeed 或 Megatron-LM 源文件。CP 序列布局、标签对齐及 aux loss 适配单独处理，不包含在本 PR 中。

## Does this PR introduce any user-facing change?

主要包括以下变化：

  - 新增可选参数 --lora-qkv-independent-a，默认关闭。开启后，Q/KV 使用初值相同但独立训练的 A 矩阵；要求 LoRA targets 包含 linear_qkv，并配置 --mla-mm-split 和 --q-lora-rank。
  - 本 PR 中独立 Q/KV A 暂要求 context_parallel_size=1；开启该功能时使用 CP>1 会明确报错，待后续 CP 适配补齐。这一限制不针对原有共享 A 路线。
  - 独立 A 当前支持普通、未融合的单 adapter LoRA，不支持 DoRA 或 adapter merge；对不兼容的配置增加检查。
  - 开启独立 A 后，adapter checkpoint 新增 lora_A_kv 参数，加载时需使用匹配配置。启用 expert bias 时，LoRA checkpoint 同时保存 router bias。
  - 并行梯度和 checkpoint 修复在对应配置下生效，可能改变原错误路径下的参数更新或加载结果；关闭独立 A 开关不会关闭这些正确性修复。

items.title: [RFC] NSA is architecturally incompatible with NVIDIA consumer/workstation GPUs — MLA is the only viable sparse attention path
items.bodyExcerpt:
### Motivation.

After extensive production testing on SM120 (RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, 8×96GB, PCIe Gen5), NSA (Native Sparse Attention) cannot be made to work reliably for production serving on NVIDIA consumer/workstation GPUs. This is not a bug — it is an architectural incompatibility.

The fundamental problems:

1. **NSA requires dynamic sparse index computation at every decode step.** This means per-layer, per-token topk selection over the full KV cache. On SM100 (datacenter Blackwell), dedicated FP8 block-scaled GEMM units handle this efficiently. On SM120, these units do not exist — the sparse indexer falls back to software paths that are both slow and correctness-problematic.

2. **PCIe topology makes NSA+MTP catastrophically unreliable.** The b12x PCIe oneshot allreduce has a buffer reuse race under CUDA graph/no-copy mode. The only known fix (a completion barrier in `pcie_oneshot.cu`) costs ~1 tok/s and still does not guarantee correctness under concurrent serving. MTP + TP>1 + concurrent>1 produces deadlocks (see #41402, #41404 — both closed without resolution).

3. **SM120 is not SM100.** FP8 block-scaled GEMM kernels written for SM100 crash or produce garbage on SM120 (#26211, #35566). FP8 KV Cache is slower than BF16 on SM120 because there are no native FP8 block-scaled compute units. NVFP4 KV Cache PRs (#21601 in SGLang) remain unmerged with critical bugs.

4. **NSA's correctness is unacceptably fragile.** The voipmonitor/GLM-5.1 reference image achieves only 93.3% accuracy (28/30), and requires a custom b12x overlay with three patched source files plus a custom vLLM tree. This is not production-grade — it is a fragile experiment.

5. **Every community Docker image for NSA+MTP is broken.** The rtx6kpro wiki images hang or produce incoherent output. Later versions are worse than earlier ones because upstream changes in both vLLM and b12x break the fragile integration points.

items.title: [RFC]: Kernel-agnostic constant-stride (layer-major) KV cache layout for KV connectors
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Motivation

#27743 added "cross-layer KV blocks" so a KV connector can stage/transfer a block's KV for
all layers at once, by allocating all layers in one tensor (`use_uniform_kv_cache` /
`allocate_uniform_kv_caches`).

For MLA backends the only supported physical layout was **block-major**
`(num_blocks, num_layers, ...)`. That makes each per-layer view a *strided* (non-contiguous)
slice, and MLA kernels require contiguous per-layer views — so #37090 **disabled cross-layer
KV for all MLA backends** (`get_kv_cache_stride_order(include_num_layers_dimension=True)`
returns the identity permutation to signal "unsupported").

The result: the cross-layer connector optimization is off for exactly the models that dominate
disaggregated prefill/decode and KV offloading today — DeepSeek V3/V3.2, GLM, Kimi, all MLA.
With it disabled, vLLM falls back to **one independent `torch.zeros` per layer**, so a connector
sees `L` allocations at unrelated base addresses. Two concrete costs:

1. The GPU↔staging layer↔page transpose needs `L` separate copies per block — there is no
   constant stride across layers to exploit.
2. RDMA connectors must register `L` memory regions (one per layer) instead of one.

## Proposed Change

Add a **second uniform layout: layer-major contiguous slices**. Allocate one buffer for all
same-spec layers and hand each layer a **contiguous slice** at a constant stride
`S = num_blocks * page_size_bytes`. The per-layer view stays contiguous and bit-identical to a
standalone tensor, so **attention kernels (including MLA) are unaffected** — no
`get_kv_cache_stride_order` support is required. This is kernel-agnostic, unlike the existing
block-major path.

```
Today — one independent torch.zeros per layer (cross-layer disabled for MLA, #37090):

  layer 0   : [ blk0 blk1 ... blkN ]   @ ptr0
  layer 1   : [ blk0 blk1 ... blkN ]   @ ptr1     (ptr1 - ptr0 : arbitrary)
   ...
  layer L-1 : [ blk0 blk1 ... blkN ]   @ ptr(L-1) (no constant stride)

  => L memory region

items.title: [RFC] LoRA Adapter Lifecycle for RL Training
items.bodyExcerpt:
# [RFC] LoRA Adapter Lifecycle for RL Training

## Problem

RL + LoRA workflows have three vLLM-side issues:

1. **sleep/wake crash**: Level-2 sleep with `enable_lora=True` crashes with KeyError — LoRA adapter parameters are not in cumem's tag set ([#39934](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/39934))
2. **Adapter-only sync missing**: frameworks must merge LoRA → send full weights → unmerge. Adapter-only sync (send only LoRA delta, load via vLLM's LoRA serving) would eliminate the merge round-trip ([trl#5975](https://github.com/huggingface/trl/issues/5975))
3. **LoRA + MoE mismatch**: logprob divergence between training and inference grows with LoRA rank on MoE models (Qwen3.6, GLM-4.7-Flash) ([SkyRL#1776](https://github.com/NovaSky-AI/SkyRL/issues/1776))

## Downstream demand

- [trl#5975](https://github.com/huggingface/trl/issues/5975): Adapter-only vLLM LoRA sync for GRPO/AsyncGRPO
- [SkyRL#1776](https://github.com/NovaSky-AI/SkyRL/issues/1776): LoRA + MoE inference mismatch investigation
- [verl#6782](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/issues/6782): Qwen3.5-27B LoRA GRPO — vLLM never emits EOS with rank=64

## Exit criterion

- sleep/wake + LoRA (#39934) no longer crashes
- Adapter-only sync path available (no full-weight merge required)

## Feedback Period

Two weeks from posting.

items.title: [Bug][ROCm] GLM-5.3-Flash kpool indexer overwrites its own KV cache: backend advertises a kernel block size the kernels do not use
items.bodyExcerpt:
### Summary

On ROCm, the GLM-5.3-Flash kpool sparse indexer **silently overwrites its own KV cache**. 4096 pool entries are written into 864 distinct slots, so ~79 % of the indexer's keys are wrong. The model still produces fluent text, so nothing crashes — long-context recall just degrades, and `temperature=0` stops being reproducible because the damage depends on which physical blocks the allocator hands out.

This is **ROCm-only** and distinct from #40018 (whose fix, #43781, is present in the tree I tested).

### Root cause

`DeepseekV32IndexerBackend.get_supported_kernel_block_sizes()` (`vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/indexer.py`):

```python
return [1, MultipleOf(16)] if current_platform.is_rocm() else [64]
```

On CUDA the backend declares exactly `[64]`, so vLLM sets `kernel_block_size = 64`, `BlockTable.use_hybrid_blocks = True`, and builds a kernel-granular block table. On ROCm it declares "any multiple of 16", so the hybrid aligner's choice (640 tokens here) is taken as natively supported: `blocks_per_kv_block == 1`, **no kernel-granular block table**.

But the kernels do not read 640-token blocks. DeepGEMM/AITER paged-MQA reads pool pages of 32 states; with `tokens_per_state == index_kpool == 4` that is 128 tokens. So the storage block (640 tok = 160 states) is five pages, and both `slot_mapping` and `cp_gather_indexer_k_quant_cache_triton` address it with the **page** size (32) while the block table holds **spec-block** ids — a 5x over-subscription.

The intended split is even documented in `vllm/models/glm5next/nvidia/attention.py` as `storage_kernel_block_size`, but that identifier appears nowhere else in the tree — it was never implemented.

### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

## Motivation

GLM-5.3-Flash (`Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration`) is a hybrid model containing both:

* sparse MLA layers
* KDA (Kimi Delta Attention / gated delta-rule) linear-attention layers

Even if GLM5Next's sparse MLA / KeyPool path is made CPU-compatible, the model still cannot execute end-to-end on CPU without a KDA backend.

I would like to request native CPU support for GLM5Next KDA.

## Current state

The GLM5Next KDA implementation currently lives under the accelerator-specific path:

```text
vllm/models/glm5next/nvidia/kda.py
```

and uses GPU-oriented Flash Linear Attention / Triton operators such as:

```text
chunk_kda_with_fused_gate
fused_recurrent_kda
```

There does not appear to be a corresponding:

```text
vllm/models/glm5next/cpu/kda.py
```

or other CPU KDA execution path for GLM5Next on current `main`.

This makes KDA an independent CPU blocker from sparse MLA / KeyPool support.

GLM-5.3-Flash has a large number of KDA layers, so this cannot reasonably be worked around by supporting only the sparse-MLA portion of the model.

The CPU backend already has substantial support for related linear-attention/state-space workloads.

In particular, current CPU platform code contains an accelerated GDN path using:

```text
AMX tiles
or

```

and vLLM already has CPU machinery for stateful hybrid models, including:

* recurrent state caches

### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

## Motivation

We operate a production vLLM deployment (GLM-based MoE model, TP=4, 4x NVIDIA B200,
V1 engine) serving a workload dominated by very long prompts (RAG/long-context,
median ~100k-180k prompt tokens per request, generation typically <1k tokens).
Under this workload we consistently observe severe TTFT tail latency caused by
head-of-line blocking in prefill scheduling, and we believe this is a strong
real-world case for reviving #49075 / #55256.

With `--enable-chunked-prefill` and `--max-num-batched-tokens` set to a

items.bodyExcerpt:
### Summary

vLLM cannot serve `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash` (or its NVFP4/FP8 quants, e.g. `nvidia/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4`). The model's MLA is **NoPE** (`qk_rope_head_dim = 0`), but `glm5_next`'s only attention backend, `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM120`, uses the `fp8_ds_mla` / `nvfp4_ds_mla` KV-cache format, whose `concat_and_cache_mla` kernel hardcodes DeepSeek geometry (`pe_dim == 64`, `kv_lora_rank == 512`). It loads, wires up TP, and profiles the KV cache successfully, then dies in MLA warmup:

```
RuntimeError: Worker failed with error 'concat_and_cache_mla, csrc/libtorch_stable/cache_kernels.cu:939, pe_dim must be 64 for fp8_ds_mla'
```

### Why it's not just the assertion

`concat_and_cache_ds_mla_kernel` launches `block(96)` = 64 threads for the 512-wide NoPE part + threads 64–95 copying exactly 64 RoPE elements into a fixed 656-byte entry. For `pe_dim=0` there is no RoPE section, so relaxing the `STD_TORCH_CHECK(pe_dim == 64, ...)` would make the RoPE threads read nonexistent `k_pe` and write a bogus rope region → silent corruption. Supporting NoPE MLA needs a dedicated kernel variant + entry layout + format routing. The same `pe_dim == 64` requirement exists in the `nvfp4_ds_mla` path, and both are still present on `main` (`csrc/libtorch_stable/cache_kernels.cu`).

### Repro

```
vllm serve nvidia/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 --distributed-executor-backend ray \
  --trust-remote-code --enforce-eager
```

> **Companion:** ROCm/aiter#3451 — required. Without it GSM8K strict-match drops 0.95 → 0.49.

`VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_DSV32_INDEXER_FUSION` (default off) + main AITER toggle; auto-disabled when the running AITER build does not expose `indexer_qk_rope_quant_and_cache`. The kernel hard-asserts `index_head_dim == 128`, `qk_rope_head_dim == 64`, `head_dim == quant_block_size`; `Indexer.__init__` only enables the path if all three hold and `model_type != "glm_moe_dsa"`.

## Design notes

- **Stays inside the existing custom op.** Calling the fused kernel from inside `rocm_aiter_sparse_attn_indexer` keeps `q_fp8` and `weights_out` from escaping — an earlier version that registered them as a separate op leaked pointers across piecewise-cudagraph segments and tanked GSM8K to ~1%.
- **Persistent workspace** for `q_fp8` / `weights_out`, grown monotonically. Otherwise 61 indexer layers × 2 allocations per decode step churn the eager allocator.
- **K stride fixup.** The kernel asserts `k.stride(0) == head_dim`, but the upstream `.contiguous()` is a no-op on `size(0) == 1` views. We rewrite the metadata via `as_strided` when it's safe, else `empty + copy_`.
- **`preshuffle=True`.** Downstream consumers read MFMA 16×16 SHUFFLE; the original call site passed `False` and silently produced garbage. Bytewise-equal to the unfused triton write after the fix.
- **fp32 LN params** passed through as-is (required by ROCm/aiter#3451).

## Correctness (GSM8K 20-shot strict-match, 1319 questions, `num_concurrent=256`)

| Configuration | strict-match |
|---|---|
| Fusion off, fp8 KV cache (baseline)

## Purpose

Fixes #46028.

When the engine fails mid-stream, the OpenAI serving layer emits an `ErrorResponse` payload (`{"error": {...}}`) via `create_streaming_error_response`, followed by `[DONE]`. The Anthropic adapter's `message_stream_converter` validated **every** chunk as a `ChatCompletionStreamResponse`, so the error chunk raised a pydantic `ValidationError`. `SiluAndMulWithClamp` routes ROCm to `forward_native`, which evaluates the activation as six eager kernels — two clamps, a sigmoid, two multiplies and an add. Follow-up to #53808.

## Background

#53808 taught `get_merged_mm_kwargs` to overlay HF-style nested
`images_kwargs` / `videos_kwargs` / `audio_kwargs` onto the flat namespace, and
threaded a `modality` argument through Qwen2-VL and Qwen3-VL. Its docstring
states the rule:

> When `modality` is set, HF-style nested `images_kwargs` / `videos_kwargs` /
> `audio_kwargs` are overlaid onto the flat namespace for vLLM-side reads

Fix a tool-calling failure mode of the glm47 parser family (GLM-4.5/4.6/4.7/5.x, incl. GLM-5.3-Flash): **the model omits a required property of a nested object when a bulky optional property precedes it in the schema**.

items.title: [Bugfix][GLM] Invalidate merged KDA convolution weights after refit
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fixes #55087.

GLM-5.3 KDA lazily merges the q/k/v convolution weights into a single cached tensor for the fused causal-conv path. During online RL or refit workflows, the underlying q/k/v convolution weights can be updated after warmup, but the derived merged tensor may remain stale. Subsequent inference can then continue using old or dummy weights even after the model weights have been refreshed.

This change:

- adds explicit invalidation for the merged KDA convolution-weight cache
- invalidates the KDA cache before GLM-5.3 model weight loading
- covers both the direct model-loading path and the top-level CausalLM loading path
- keeps the merged-weight cache for normal inference when weights are unchanged

items.title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Stop dummy draft decode steps from writing KV through stale block-table rows
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fix a KV-cache corruption in Model Runner V2 speculative decoding under data parallelism: an idle DP rank's dummy batch runs the drafter's multi-step decode, which computes real slot mappings through the *persistent* per-slot block tables using `idx_mapping = arange(num_reqs)` (real request-state slots whose rows are stale), and writes drafter-layer K/V into offsets `1..k-1` of the first block of whatever request last occupied those slots. Those blocks are typically already registered in the prefix cache, so every later request that hits them reads corrupted drafter K/V while the target model's K/V stays intact.

Observed on GLM-5.2 (glm_moe_dsa, MTP k=5, DP=4 EP, prefix caching) as a per-request, exactly-zero MTP acceptance (`p0 = 0.0000`, `acc_len = 1.0`, `drafts == max_tokens`) that latches onto a conversation and disappears after `POST /reset_prefix_cache`; the poisoned rows were NaN (fp8 `0x7F`) in `model.layers.78.self_attn.attn`, with the target layers and indexer cache of the same block clean. On current main the same stale write still happens on every idle step (the written values happen to be finite there, so acceptance is unaffected), i.e. the write path is latent.

#49757 protected the read side (`get_dummy_block_tables` zeroes `input_block_tables`) and the target's dummy slot mappings are PAD (`prepare_dummy_attn`), but `_compute_slot_mappings_kernel` reads `block_table_ptrs` (the persistent tables), which neither protection covers.

## Fix

- `_compute_slot_mappings_kernel`: a row with `idx_mapping < 0` (dummy or CUDA-graph padding request) emits `PAD_SLOT_ID` and never dereferences a negative block-table row.
- `AutoRegressiveSpeculator.propose(dummy_run=True)`: mark every dummy row with `idx_mapping = -1` (already the speculator's convention for padded rows, ignored by `gumbel_sample`).

The guard lives in the kernel rather than in Python because the fused multi-step path re-runs `compute_slot_mappings` inside the captured CU

items.title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Skip non-prefix-cacheable groups in SimpleCPUOffload (GLM-5.3-Flash kpool tail and QSA)
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

GLM-5.3-Flash carries a kpool-tail scratch group (`KpoolTailSpec`, `prefix_cacheable=False`, `block_size=index_kpool=4`) next to prefix-cacheable groups that hash at 1152 tokens on this box (MLA 1152, 4× Mamba 1152 in `align` mode). Core (`resolve_kv_cache_block_sizes`, `HybridKVCacheCoordinator`, `KVCacheManager`) and the `MooncakeStore connector` already skip such groups. `SimpleCPUOffloadScheduler` did not, and treated every KV cache group as offloadable:

- `_select_eager_blocks_to_store` views the request hashes at each group's block size to build `BlockStored` metadata. For the tail group that is `resolve_block_hashes(hashes, hash_block_size=1152, block_size=4)`, which trips the divisibility assert as soon as `--kv-events-config` enables KV cache events. The engine dies on the first prefill store.
- `update_state_after_alloc` maps external (CPU-hit) tokens onto the scratch group and asserts alignment against its block size, although the coordinator never returns hit blocks for it.

This PR records which groups take part in offloading (`prefix_cacheable`) and skips the rest in eager store selection and in load pairing. Scratch blocks never carry a hash, so nothing is stored or loaded for them either way; the scratch slot in the per-group hit tuple stays empty, exactly as the coordinator leaves it.


## Duplication check

Two open PRs touch the same code path: #55033 (draft since 2026-09-02, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next QSA ring, also adjusts `_estimate_lazy_target_blocks`) and #56404 (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, gates `resolve_block_hashes` in the store path only, currently conflicting). This PR is scoped to the GLM-5.3-Flash kpool-tail layout and adds what neither of them covers: a regression test for the actual crash trigger (`enable_kv_cache_events=true`, `BlockStored` emitted for cacheable groups only) and an end-to-end store/load + accuracy check on GLM-5.3-Flash. Happy to fold the test into #55033 instead if the maintainers prefer to land that one.

items.title: [ROCm][Model][DCP] Default Kimi-K3's DCP combine to a2a
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Kimi-K3 leaves `dcp_comm_backend` unset, so it gets the `ag_rs` default: `allgather(lse)` + `reduce_scatter(out)`. The `a2a` combine is a single `all_to_all_single` and is faster at every token count measured.

Wall ms per combine call, MI355X (gfx950, 8-rank xGMI):

| tokens | `ag_rs` | `a2a` | speedup |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 5 | 0.107 | 0.095 | 1.13x |
| 48 | 0.111 | 0.097 | 1.15x |
| 144 | 0.136 | 0.101 | **1.35x** |

The margin grows with T, and combine runs **per MLA layer per decode step**, so it multiplies by the layer count. Cosine similarity against `ag_rs` was **>= 0.999994** across the sweep.

`GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM` already does exactly this through the same `set_dcp_defaults` hook, added in #50382. This applies the same treatment to Kimi-K3.

Three deliberate limits on scope:

- **ROCm only.** The hook returns early off ROCm. `a2a` is one `all_to_all_single` against `allgather(lse)` + `reduce_scatter(out)`, so which side wins depends on the interconnect, and the numbers above are MI355X (gfx950, 8-rank xGMI). No other platform's default is moved by this change. Both branches are covered by tests.

- **`q_replicate` is not set.** `GlmMoeDsa` pairs `a2a` with `q_replicate=True`; that changes weight loading and is an independent question we have not measured, so it is left alone.
- **This changes only the default.** `set_dcp_defaults` fills options the user left unset, so an explicit `--dcp-comm-backend` still wins. A test pins that, because a "default" that silently overrode the flag would be worse than no default at all.

`a2a` has a known caveat under PCP: #56677 pins `--dcp-comm-backend ag_rs` for a GLM-5.2 PCP4+DCP4 eval config, and GLM already defaults to `a2a`. items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fix a start-up crash of GLM-5.3-Flash in data-parallel deployments (TP=1 per rank): `fused_recurrent_gated_delta_rule_fwd_kernel` was launched with `grid = (NK, NV, N * HV)`, and with 64 KDA value heads on one GPU the first CUDA-graph capture batch of 1024 sequences needs `1024 * 64 = 65536` programs — one over the CUDA `gridDim.z` limit of 65535 — so the launch fails with `Triton Error [CUDA]: invalid argument` and `--data-parallel-size 4` (with or without EP) cannot start. TP4 (16 heads per rank) is unaffected.

The kernel now carries `N * HV` in `gridDim.x` (limit 2^31-1) with the `program_id` mapping swapped accordingly. The same launch pattern is mirrored in the AMD copy and in the flash-linear-attention copies (`fused_recurrent.py`, `fused_sigmoid_gating.py`, `kda.py`), which are changed the same way. The packed-decode kernel in the same file already guarded this case (`split_batch_head_grid = B * HV > 65535`).

Fixes #56973

## Why this is not duplicating an existing PR

Searched vllm-project/vllm open and closed PRs and issues (GitHub search, 2026-09-13 and 2026-09-15) for `fused_recurrent_kda`, `gridDim.z`, `65535`, `invalid argument` + GLM-5.3-Flash / KDA / DP: no report of this crash and no PR touching the launch grid of `fused_recurrent_gated_delta_rule_fwd_kernel`; the only related guard is the existing `split_batch_head_grid` check in the packed-decode kernel of the same file.

items.title: [ROCm][Bugfix] Support FP8 KV cache for NoPE sparse MLA
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Summary

- route rope-free sparse MLA to the ROCm Triton implementation for every KV-cache dtype
- dequantize FP8 KV rows in the Triton ragged-prefill kernel using the layer KV scale while keeping Q in model dtype
- use 64-bit query-row offsets so wide, long-context prefills cannot overflow 32-bit pointer arithmetic
- preserve custom MLA geometry and FP8 cache dtype in the attention benchmark harness

## Problem

AITER precompiled sparse MLA kernels assume the DeepSeek cache-row geometry: 512 latent elements plus 64 RoPE elements. GLM-5.3-Flash is rope-free and stores a 512-element row. items.bodyExcerpt:
Reviving #55256's clean threshold-independent `max_concurrent_prefills` limit for the V1 scheduler to fix the exact head-of-line blocking issue reported in #57413.

As detailed in #57413, without a cap on concurrent partial prefills, long-context RAG workloads (e.g. 100k+ tokens) completely stall V1's scheduling queue. Short requests are forced to wait for many iterations until massive partial prefills finish.

This reintroduces `max_concurrent_prefills` directly into the V1 scheduler's `WAITING` loop. By bounding how many requests can simultaneously hold partial prefill state, we allow interleaving and dramatically reduce tail TTFT (as validated by the community on 4x B200 / GLM-5.3-Flash).

Original patch credit to @fululi12 in #55256. Rebased and verified against main.

[Security] Bound OpenCV video decode frame walks
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Summary
The default OpenCV video decoder walks every source frame up to the last sampled index via sequential `cap.grab()`. Uniform sampling always includes that last index, so decode CPU tracks container frame count rather than the small number of returned frames. A long, highly compressible video stays under the download-size cap and can occupy a media worker for the full walk. This adds `VLLM_MAX_VIDEO_DECODE_FRAMES` (default 36000, `0` disables) and rejects over-budget walks before either OpenCV grab loop starts.

## Changes
- `vllm/envs.py`: add `VLLM_MAX_VIDEO_DECODE_FRAMES`.
- `vllm/multimodal/video_decoders/base.py`: reject walks above the cap.
- `vllm/multimodal/video_decoders/opencv.py`: enforce the cap in `read_frames` (covers recovery and non-recovery paths).
- `docs/usage/security.md`: document the new decode-size guard.
- Tests for under-limit, over-limit (both recovery modes), disable-with-0, and the `VideoMediaIO` entry point.

## Codepath coverage
- Chat / messages / responses / batch / `/invocations` / gRPC / offline `LLM.generate` all reach `VideoMediaIO` → OpenCV `read_frames`: covered.
- `video/jpeg` base64 and TorchCodec / PyNvVideoCodec / DeepStream do not use this grab loop: N/A.

## Purpose

GLM-5.3-Flash sparse-MLA models keep a one-block-per-request circular tail cache (kpool). Every decode step — twice per step with MTP, once for the target model and once for the drafter — `KpoolTailMetadataBuilder.build()` maps each token to its request's tail ring with a chain of small torch ops (`arange` + `searchsorted` + `clamp` + `index_select` + `remainder` + `copy_`): 12 kernel launches and ~250 us of CPU enqueue time per build.

## Purpose

  Fixes #54359: GLM-5.3-Flash kpool indexer overwrites its own KV cache.

  On ROCm, GLM-5.3-Flash compresses one indexer state from every
  index_kpool tokens. However, the generic ROCm indexer backend currently
  advertises the following kernel block-size support in token units:

  [1, MultipleOf(16)]

  This allows the complete KV manager block to be selected directly as the
  kernel block size.

  used by the kernel.

items.bodyExcerpt:
### What does this PR do?

HF video processors take `videos` and a parallel `video_metadata` kwarg. vLLM's parser instead bundles metadata into each item as `(frames, metadata)` so it travels with the video through hashing and caching. Nothing in between reconciles the two, so every model that needs metadata unzips the tuples itself, and each does it differently:

| file | behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| `glm4_1v.py` | converts to `VideoMetadata`, hoists `do_sample_frames` (last one wins) |
| `ernie45_vl.py` | gated on `supports_video_metadata`, warns and unwraps for old processors |
| `molmo2.py` | asserts the tuple shape, reads `frames_indices` for timestamps |
| `llava_onevision2.py` | recovers a codec file path from a private marker key in the metadata dict |

items.title: kv-cache: honor scheduler lookahead in mamba align-mode allocation
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Problem

In mamba align cache mode (mamba-hybrid models with prefix caching), `MambaManager.allocate_new_blocks` and `get_num_blocks_to_allocate` discarded all lookahead tokens by resetting `num_tokens` to `num_tokens_main_model`. When the scheduler schedules lookahead capacity beyond a main-model sequence that ends exactly on a page boundary, this corrupts the recurrent state in two ways.

## Root cause

A mamba state table row is page-indexed: the worker's running-state column is `cdiv(main_end, bs) - 1`.

1. **Missing next page.** When a chunk ends exactly on a page boundary and lookahead tokens extend beyond it, the next page was not materialized with the current schedule. The boundary token's state write then targeted a block-table entry that still held a recycled stale block — the recurrent state is corrupted from that point on (one-step NaN followed by a repetition lock at every page boundary).

2. **Displaced running-state column.** If a page was materialized for the lookahead, the null padding was derived from the inflated `num_tokens`, so the reserved page displaced the real running-state column. The worker's running-state index (0 for a chunk ending at the first page boundary) pointed at the null slot; the next chunk's state pre-copy chained from the null slot and spec-decode acceptance collapsed to zero permanently for that request.

## Diagnosis

Reproduced on a 4-node Arm (Thor SM110) cluster serving GLM-5.3-Flash (mamba-hybrid + MTP + prefix caching) with deterministic single-turn probes: prompts whose prefill chunk ends exactly on a page boundary produced 0% spec-decode acceptance from the first decode step, while boundary-crossing-free prompts were healthy. The failure moved with cache layout across boots, and per-request scheduler dumps of the mamba state-table rows showed the displaced null column exactly at the worker's running-state index. The corruption was confirmed to chain through the state pre-copy (pre-copy source = the null slot).

## Purpose

Rather than updating every call site to pass `force_fp32_compute` (only nemotron_h does today), self-enable inside `GateLinear`: when `is_gfx950 and (input_size, output_size) in ROCM_FP32_ROUTER_GEMM_SUPPORTED_SHAPES and not bias`, set `force_fp32_compute = True` so the existing logic stores fp32 weights. - Unsupported shapes on gfx950 (e.g. GLM-5.3-Flash's `(4096, 288)`): `is_rocm_fp32_shape` false, clean fallback.
- Biased gates: guard excludes bias (kernel/torch.mm path has no bias term).

No GPU locally, so verified by simulation of the exact decision tree in `GateLinear.__init__`:

| Case | weights | fp32 kernel |
|---|---|---|
| gfx950, (6144, 256), no bias (issue repro) | fp32 | **enabled** (was: unreachable) |
| gfx950, (4096, 288) (GLM-5.3-Flash) | bf16 | unchanged fallback |

items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fixes #55087. GLM-5.3 KDA merges the q/k/v short-conv weights into one cached tensor (`_merged_conv_weight`), built lazily on first forward. Online-RL workflows warm up with dummy weights (cache built), then refit `q_conv1d`/`k_conv1d`/`v_conv1d` — but the cached merge is never invalidated, so inference silently keeps using the pre-refit convolution weights.

## Approach

Weight loading dispatches on the param's stamped `weight_loader` (`getattr(param, "weight_loader", default_weight_loader)` in `AutoWeightsLoader`). So the cache can be invalidated at exactly the point the weights change: in `Glm5NextLinearAttention.__init__`, wrap each conv weight's stamped loader so any write clears `_merged_conv_weight`. - ✅ Initial load (loaders run before first forward; cache built after anyway)

items.title: [Bugfix] Skip FP8-dequant fast paths for PP-missing layers in GLM-5.3-Flash load
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fixes #55725. GLM-5.3-Flash crashes at weight load on multi-node (2×8 H100) with `KeyError: 'layers.11.self_attn.fused_qkv_a_proj.weight'` on every second-node worker, while single-node runs fine.

## Root cause

With 2 nodes the run is pipeline-parallel (PP=2), so layer 11's params exist only on stage-0 ranks. The attached log (`layer11.log`) shows all `Worker_PP1_TP0..7` crashing; PP0 is clean. The normal load path guards every weight with `is_pp_missing_parameter` (glm5next/common/model.py), but the two FP8-dequant fast paths bypass it and index `params_dict` directly:

- `_try_load_fp8_attn_proj` → `params_dict[target_w]` (the traceback in the issue)
- `_try_load_fp8_indexer_wk` → `params_dict[fused_name]` (same class of hole)

On a PP rank that doesn't hold the layer, `params_dict` has no such key → KeyError before the normal path ever gets a chance to skip the weight.

## Fix

In both fast paths, return `False` when the target param is absent from `params_dict`, so the weight falls through to the normal path, which skips it via `is_pp_missing_parameter`. The indexer-wk guard is placed *before* buffering, so PP ranks also don't accumulate fp8 tensors that nobody loads. Behavior on ranks that hold the layer is byte-identical.

## Verification

No multi-node GPU here, so verified by driving both functions directly with the exact crashing weight names, on the MI350X pod against the patched module:

| Case | Result |
|---|---|
| PP1-style params_dict (layer 11 absent), fp8 `q_a_proj` weight + scale | not consumed, nothing loaded → falls to normal skip path (was: KeyError) |
| PP0-style control (BF16 `fused_qkv_a_proj` present) | consumed + loaded, unchanged |
| PP1, indexer `wk` weight + scale | not consumed → normal skip |
| PP0 control, indexer `wk` | consumed + loaded, unchanged |

items.title: [KV-Offloading][TP] : Expand replicated_layout detection to multi-group MLA
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose
KV offloading for MLA models + TP need only offload KV values from one TP rank. 
This is controlled by replicated_layout determination in `vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/offloading/config.py`

Building on top of @almogtavor 's work https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50667 (which was eventually closed) , this PR expand the replicated_layout check to include, 
 - SlidingWindowMLASpec
 - Multi-group MLASpec / SlidingWindowMLASpec
 models. 
 
Notably, 
- deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash
- deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp and 
- zai-org/GLM-5.3
fall in this category. 

### Changes:
 - in the replicated_layout check, 
   * Unwrap `UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs` and check that the internal layer specs are MLA
   * Check if all the layer_spec in all the Attention groups are in [MLAAttentionSpec, SlidingWindowMLASpec]
   * Additionally, check that the advertises `num_kv_heads = 1`, indicating TP sharding of KV heads is not possible. 
   * Remove the existing size check 
   ```
        and worker_kv_bytes_per_block
        == single_group_spec.page_size_bytes
        * len(kv_cache_config.kv_cache_groups[0].layer_names)
   ```
    this is critical and loosens the existing conditions on `main` . This is because the KV cache groups are flattened in the Scheduler process here https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/038cb14bd7874030e98bb6edc4b6f4efe649fff7/vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py#L2376 . 
    Specifically, the realization of the comment, 
    ```
            # All layers in the UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs have the same type,
            # so use an arbitrary one to initialize the scheduler.
    ```
    makes it impossible to compute the correct size from the KVCache groups to correctly effect this "size" sanity check. Groups such as
